result.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Evidence Misgrounding in Multimodal Knowledge Editing
result.summary: Multimodal knowledge editing aims to update visually grounded facts in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) while preserving unrelated text and visual behaviors. However, standard answer-level metrics can hide evidence misgrounding: an edit may produce the target answer on the original image yet remain sensitive to incidental context rather than the intended visual evidence. To examine this issue in a controlled setting, we construct WaterBird-Edit, an analysis set that decouples bird habitat labels from background context and measures whether edited predictions remain stable when the target evidence is preserved but the background changes. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose VICE (Visual In-Context Editing), a retrieval-based framework that stores edits in external memory and applies them through visual in-context demonstrations designed to expose task-relevant evidence. Experiments on three standard benchmarks show that VICE achieves strong lifelong editing performance, while results on WaterBird-Edit show that it substantially reduces sensitivity to the controlled background shifts. Code and dataset are available in https://github.com/Wang-Z-W/VICE-main.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出多模态知识编辑存在「证据误接地」：答案级指标可能掩盖编辑后的预测其实依赖偶发背景而非目标视觉证据；为此构建 WaterBird-Edit，将鸟类栖息地标签与背景解耦，并检验背景变化时预测是否稳定，同时提出基于外部记忆检索与视觉上下文示范的 VICE 框架来缓解该问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以保持目标证据、替换背景的方式检验答案是否真正使用目标视觉信息，与 LVR 关注的视觉旁路、证据筛选及「答案是否用了视觉内容」的评价问题直接相关，其指标与数据构造可供核查。
